tasks.final_text: Back in the day, the romans beleived strongly in the gods and in omens. They had a practice where,  before battle, they'd take some chickens, and put food in front of them, and if the chickens ate the food, that was a good omen and they'd proceed to battle. If the chickens did not eat, they would take that as a bad omen and retreat.

The 1954 Atlantic hurricate season was an above-average Atlantic hurricane season in terms of named storms, with 16 forming. Overall the season resulted in $751.6 million in damage, the most of any season at the time. The season officially began on June 15, and nine days later the first named storm developed.
